equation_request.abstract: The quantum Fourier transform (QFT) is a key ingredient of several quantum algorithms and a qudit-specific implementation of the QFT is hence an important step toward the realization of qudit-based quantum computers. This work develops a circuit decomposition of the QFT for hybrid qudits based on generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates, which can be implemented using selective rotations in NMR. We experimentally implement the hybrid qudit QFT on an NMR quantum emulator, which uses four qubits to emulate a single qutrit coupled to two qubits.

specification.problem: QFT over Z_12 on a hybrid register of one qutrit (d1=3) and two qubits (d2=d3=2), built from generalized Hadamards (F_d) and generalized controlled-phase gates. The qutrit is encoded in 2 qubits, so 4 physical qubits are used. The circuit has no oracle and no measurement in the unitary/statevector check.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One instance: N=12=3*2*2 with the qutrit as the most significant input digit. The deliverable is the exact circuit unitary on the 12-dimensional valid subspace of the 16-dimensional space. The output is labelled in digit-reversed order (qutrit register holds the least significant output digit). Outside this scope: the paper's NMR selective-rotation pulse sequences, the experiment and its fidelities, general mixed dimensions, and a physical qutrit.

symbols.meaning: Input integer; digits x_1 in Z_3 (qutrit), x_2,x_3 in Z_2
Output integer; y_1 in Z_3 on the qutrit register, y_2,y_3 in Z_2 on the qubits
Primitive cube root of unity exp(2 pi i/3)
Qutrit level, encoded on qubits (q_0,q_1) as l=q_0+2q_1; level 3 (q_0=q_1=1) is unused

equations.label: Target transform
equations.description: Z_12 QFT that the hybrid circuit must realize on the valid subspace, with y read as y_1+3y_2+6y_3 from the registers (qutrit, qubit 2, qubit 3).
equations.justification: The abstract names the QFT for hybrid qudits; the Z_N DFT is its standard definition.

equations.label: Mixed-radix phase factorization
equations.description: With x=4x_1+2x_2+x_3 and y=y_1+3y_2+6y_3, the DFT phase splits into one Hadamard-type term per digit plus controlled-phase terms between a processed digit and later digits.
equations.justification: Direct expansion of x*y/12, dropping integer parts. It gives the decomposition Hadamard then controlled phases, as in the qubit QFT. Qutrit-first ordering forces the output digit order (y_1,y_2,y_3).
assumptions: Qutrit is the most significant input digit

equations.label: Generalized Hadamard
equations.description: Gate on the qutrit encoding qubits (levels 0,1,2 as 00,01,10 with identity on the unused level 3) and the qubit Hadamard. F_3 is compiled from two-level Givens rotations on levels 0-1 and 1-2 plus phases.
equations.abstract_quote: based on generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates, which can be implemented using selective rotations in NMR
equations.justification: The generalized Hadamard of dimension d is the d-point DFT matrix. The Givens-rotation compilation is a construction choice, not specified in the abstract.
assumptions: Compilation into standard Qiskit rotations and multi-controlled gates is left to the circuit builder; any exact decomposition of F_3 is acceptable

equations.label: Qutrit-to-qubit controlled phases
equations.latex: C_{1k}=\sum_{l,b}e^{2\pi i\, l b/(3\cdot 2^{k-1}\cdot\,2)}|l\rangle\langle l|\otimes|b\rangle\langle b|,\ k=2,3\ (\text{angles }2\pi lb/6,\ 2\pi lb/12)
equations.description: Phase exp(2 pi i y_1 x_k/(3*2^{k-1})) with y_1 the qutrit level and x_k the qubit value. Since l=q_0+2q_1, this equals CP(2 pi/6 or 2 pi/12) from q_0 plus CP(2 times that angle) from q_1 onto the target qubit; the action on the unused level 3 is irrelevant.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_2 and linearity in l. It is a proposed implementation of the generalized controlled-phase gate and is simpler than the multi-controlled-phase form in the sketch.
assumptions: Only the valid subspace is checked

equations.label: Qubit-qubit controlled phase
equations.description: Implements the phase exp(2 pi i y_2 x_3/4).
equations.justification: Standard qubit-QFT controlled phase, with the angle from eq_2.

registers.name: qutrit
registers.role: Holds x_1 at input and y_1 at output

registers.name: qubit2
registers.role: Holds x_2 at input and y_2 at output

registers.name: qubit3
registers.role: Holds x_3 at input and y_3 at output

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state with qutrit level x_1, qubit2 = x_2, qubit3 = x_3. The Qiskit statevector index is x_1+4*x_2+8*x_3. This index differs from x=4x_1+2x_2+x_3, so convert digits explicitly.

steps.description: Apply F_3 on the qutrit register (q0,q1), identity on level 3.
Apply the controlled phases from the qutrit to qubit2 (angle 2pi/6 per level) and to qubit3 (angle 2pi/12 per level), each as CP gates from q0 and q1 (q1 with twice the angle).
Apply H on qubit2, then CP(pi/2) between qubit2 and qubit3.
Apply H on qubit3. No final swap is applied, because the output is already in (y_1,y_2,y_3) order.

specification.measurement: None for the unitary/statevector check. For a counts variant, measure all 4 qubits and decode y_1=q0+2*q1, y_2=q2, y_3=q3 (Qiskit bit 0 is rightmost in the key), then y=y_1+3y_2+6y_3.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the statevector amplitude at output digits (y_1,y_2,y_3) with exp(2 pi i x y/12)/sqrt(12) for y=y_1+3y_2+6y_3, and check zero weight on the unused level 11 of the qutrit. For a periodic input, peaks appear at multiples of 12/period.
assumptions: Qutrit is the most significant input digit
The runner checks the valid 12-dimensional subspace
Output digit order is reversed relative to input significance
Selective rotations are compiled into standard Qiskit gates
missing_information: The paper's exact selective-rotation decomposition of F_3 and the controlled-phase gates
Whether a final permutation to standard output order y=4a+2b+c is required
